skill.name: seedance-v2
skill.description: Generate short cinematic videos with ByteDance Seedance 2.0 Pro through the RunComfy CLI. The skill documents inputs, prompt patterns, limits, and model routing.
skill.summary: Create short Seedance 2.0 Pro videos with RunComfy prompts, reference media guidance, and CLI invocation details.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: Most high-severity static findings are false positives from Markdown code spans, placeholder URLs, and documented token storage. The skill does require executing the RunComfy CLI and sending prompts or media references to a third-party API. No evidence of prompt injection or credential exfiltration was found.

remediation.issue: External CLI execution and global installation are required.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for explicit user confirmation before installing or running the RunComfy CLI, and prefer pinned or verified CLI versions.

remediation.issue: Prompts and media references are sent to RunComfy.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before upload and advise them not to submit confidential prompts, private media, or restricted customer assets.

remediation.issue: Authentication setup stores a local API token.
remediation.suggestion: State that the skill must never read, print, or transmit the token file and should rely on the CLI or RUNCOMFY_TOKEN only.

remediation.issue: Placeholder URLs trigger path traversal scanner noise.
remediation.suggestion: Replace https://... placeholders with example.com media URLs to reduce false positive static findings.

content.value_statement: Teams need clear guidance for short cinematic video generation without guessing endpoint limits. This skill guides Seedance 2.0 Pro prompts, media references, and RunComfy CLI use.
actual_capabilities: Invokes the RunComfy CLI for bytedance/seedance-v2/pro with a structured input body.
Documents required and optional inputs, including prompt, media references, duration, aspect ratio, resolution, and seed.
Explains when Seedance is the better route than HappyHorse, Wan, Kling, or LTX.
Provides prompt guidance for identity references, camera motion, audio direction, and lip-sync.
Lists endpoint limits, expected exit codes, and troubleshooting references.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI and an authenticated RunComfy account or token.
Generated clips are limited to 4 to 15 seconds on this endpoint.
Reference video and audio files must meet length and size limits.

use_cases.title: Create spokesperson ads
use_cases.description: Build short lip-synced ads from a character image, concise copy, and a vertical video format.

use_cases.title: Draft cinematic previs shots
use_cases.description: Turn scene references and camera direction into short clips for review before production.

use_cases.title: Test branded video variants
use_cases.description: Compare short clips with fixed seeds, aspect ratios, and reference assets for campaign selection.

prompt_templates.title: Basic text video
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple short clip.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 5 second Seedance 2.0 Pro video from this idea: [describe the scene]. Use natural motion and clear lighting.

prompt_templates.title: Reference image ad
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request using one stable character or product image.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a vertical Seedance ad using my reference image for identity. The scene should show [action], with [tone] speech and soft camera movement.

prompt_templates.title: Multi-modal scene
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with image, video, and audio references.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the image for subject identity, the video for scene layout, and the audio for voice tone. Create a short cinematic shot with [camera direction].

prompt_templates.title: Variant testing plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced campaign workflow with repeatable creative options.
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare three Seedance 2.0 Pro variants for [campaign goal]. Keep the same reference assets, vary camera movement, and note the best seed strategy.

output_examples.input: A marketer asks for a vertical cafe spokesperson ad using one product image.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a concise Seedance prompt, recommends 8 seconds, selects 9:16, and tells the user to use the product image.

output_examples.input: A filmmaker asks to combine a scene clip and a voice reference for a short test shot.
output_examples.output: The skill checks media length limits, routes the request to Seedance 2.0 Pro, and provides camera and audio direction for the clip.

output_examples.input: A user asks for one 30 second generated video.
output_examples.output: The skill explains the 15 second endpoint limit and suggests splitting the concept into shorter connected segments.

best_practices: Use image references for stable identity and prompt text for motion, mood, and camera.
Confirm that prompts and media references are allowed to be shared with RunComfy before running the CLI.
Keep duration, resolution, and reference media within the endpoint limits.
anti_patterns: Do not describe stable faces or logos only in text when an image reference is available.
Do not mix conflicting visual styles or camera directions in one short prompt.
Do not request clips longer than 15 seconds from this endpoint.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps generate short Seedance 2.0 Pro videos through the RunComfy CLI.

faq.question: Does it require a RunComfy account?
faq.answer: Yes. Users need the RunComfy CLI and either browser login or a RUNCOMFY_TOKEN value.

faq.question: Can it use reference media?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented endpoint accepts image, video, and audio references within stated limits.

faq.question: What are the output limits?
faq.answer: The endpoint supports 4 to 15 second clips at 480p or 720p.

faq.question: Does it upload my content?
faq.answer: Yes. Prompts and reference media URLs are sent to RunComfy when the CLI is run.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
